metadata.title: PISA 2018 Results (Volume V) (EN) : Effective Policies, Successful Schools

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2018 volume reports results based on the PISA 2018 assessment of 15-year-olds across 79 countries/economies. The Reader’s Guide states that when principals’ questionnaire responses are presented, they are weighted so that they are proportionate to the number of 15-year-olds enrolled in the school, indicating the use of complex survey weighting at least for school-level questionnaire aggregation. The excerpt does not provide the specific student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For analysts using the PISA database, the standard practice is to apply the provided sampling/survey weights and replicate weights (if available) when estimating means, differences, and regression-based associations, and to use the OECD/PISA guidance for combining estimates across plausible values.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable here because the provided text is an OECD volume describing PISA 2018 results and policy implications rather than reporting an empirical ML model that explicitly uses PV-based achievement as a dependent variable. The excerpt also does not document a specific missing-data handling strategy for any statistical model (e.g., PV combining rules, imputation, or deletion rules), so missing-data handling cannot be verified from the supplied content. This is therefore a reporting gap for the purposes of extracting ML/PV/missing-data methodology details.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2018 target population of 15-year-old students (aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months) enrolled in school and having completed at least 6 years of formal schooling, across the 79 participating countries/economies. The excerpt does not specify additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade bands, subsamples, or exclusions beyond PISA’s standard exclusion criteria), so the analytic sample is treated as the full available PISA 2018 population for the reported indicators. The Reader’s Guide notes that overall exclusion rates are kept below 5% within countries to limit distortion of national mean scores, and that school-level and student-level exclusions can occur for technical reasons (e.g., remote/small schools, language proficiency, intellectual disability).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD volume reports PISA 2018 results (Volume V: Effective Policies, Successful Schools) for 15-year-olds across 79 countries/economies, focusing on how school organisation, resources, governance, and assessment practices relate to performance, equity, and student well-being. The assessment is computer-based in most systems, with reading as the main subject and mathematics/science/global competence as additional components; students complete a two-hour test with multi-stage adaptive reading item assignment and different test forms. Students also complete a background questionnaire (about 35 minutes) and school principals complete a school questionnaire (about 45 minutes), with optional teacher/parent/student well-being and other modules in subsets of countries. The excerpt provides multiple policy-relevant associations and descriptive comparisons (e.g., disadvantaged students’ reading differences, staff/material shortages, online learning platform access, and links between learning time and reading performance), but it does not present an ML modeling pipeline with explicit PV/missing-data handling details. Therefore, the extraction is limited to assessment design and high-level findings rather than ML-specific methodological results.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA results volume rather than an empirical ML paper: it synthesizes cross-country PISA 2018 evidence and reports policy-oriented associations and descriptive statistics. As a result, there is no student-level ML training/evaluation, no explicit PV-combining or missing-data imputation strategy for an ML model in the provided excerpt, and no per-country analytic sample sizes are reported in the text shown. The extraction therefore sets ML fields to empty and uses the Reader’s Guide and executive summary to document the assessment framework and the nature of the reported outcomes.
